claims.value: SILAC light = pre-existing proteins; SILAC heavy = proteins synthesised during the labelling period (same culture, same run)
claims.evidence: Paper Methods/PRIDE protocol: "quiescent fibroblasts were switched to media containing stable heavy isotopes of lysine and arginine (13C6-Lysine, 13C6, 15N4-Arginine) for 1 to 6 days"; Fig. 1 legend: % 12C ("old") remaining vs % 13C-labelled ("new"). Supp Data 1: "%heavy isotope ... after 0, 2, 4 and 6 days of labeling". Data check (heavy_frac): passing heavy-search PSMs rise with labelling time in every file (WT 0D ~1%, 1D 27%, 2D 36-37%, 4D 50-53%, 6D 58-61%; HGPS 0D 2-18%, 1D 29-32%, 2D 44-48%, 4D 76%, 6D 71-77%) and Supp Data 1 median %heavy WT 5.3/28.0/45.9/60.5, HGPS 2.1/41.2/64.6/77.8 at 0/2/4/6 D -> heavy = new. Both channels come from one culture, so they share biological replicate 1 and get distinct source names (precedent PXD028934). 0D rows: heavy channel kept because each 0D run was searched for heavy peptides and Supp Data 1 has a 0D sheet (background control).

claims.location: characteristics[sampling time], factor value[sampling time], characteristics[subcellular fraction], factor value[subcellular fraction], characteristics[cellular component] rows 1-20
claims.value: N day from file name (0D,1D,2D,4D,6D); nuclear extract / nuclear pellet; nucleus
claims.evidence: Run names <date>_HGPS_<N>D_<extract|pellet>[_2].ms2 and mzid names HGPS_<N>D_<extract|pellet>.mzid. PRIDE/paper: "Crude nuclei were extracted in 10 mM Tris pH 8, 1% n-octyl glucoside, 400 mM NaCl, and 1 mM DTT, and extracts and pellets were prepared separately for LC-MS/MS". Sampling time = days in heavy medium before harvest; confirmed by the monotonic heavy fraction (heavy_frac). cellular component nucleus = GO:0005634. Extract and pellet are distinct measured samples -> characteristics + factor (rule 16); characteristics[subcellular fraction] is a custom column (curated precedent name).
One labelling culture per time point; each (time, fraction) group contains one culture (rule 3). Files with suffix _2 are repeat injections -> comment[technical replicate] 2.

RawConverter .ms2 files were renamed: mzid SpectraData point to MHAB-N mzXMLs. LastScan/scanCount matches: HGPS_0D_extract=MHAB-11_MP (102188), HGPS_0D_pellet=MHAB-12_MP (114244), HGPS_2D_extract=MHAB-15_SCX (121333), HGPS_2D_pellet=MHAB-16_SCX (122099), HGPS_4D_pellet=MHAB-18_MP (122368; first precursor 425.77 identical), HGPS_6D_extract=MHAB-19_SCX (121430), HGPS_6D_pellet=MHAB-20_SCX (124193), HGPS_1D_extract=MHAB-13_SCX (120795), HGPS_1D_pellet=MHAB-14_SCX (121192; first precursor 254.98 identical), HGPS_4D_extract=MHAB-17_SCX (121011). Each mzid HGPS_<N>D_<fraction> points to the MHAB-N file mapped to the same-named .ms2. All 10 .ms2 and 10 mzXML pair 1:1.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; Phospho S,T,Y variable; Label:13C(6) K; Label:13C(6)15N(4) R
claims.evidence: Each mzIdentML holds two SpectrumIdentificationProtocols (IP2/ProLuCID): SIP_ for light spectra and SIP_H for the "H"-prefixed copy of the same mzXML. SIP_H adds fixed +6.0201 K (MOD:00544, 13C6 Lys = UNIMOD:188 Label:13C(6)) and +10.0083 R (MOD:00587, 13C6 15N4 Arg = UNIMOD:267 Label:13C(6)15N(4)); in the SDRF the label masses are written MT=Variable (campaign rule 11). Carbamidomethyl = 57.02146 C (MOD:00397), paper "Carbamidomethylation on cysteine was considered as a static modification". The 0D, 2D and 6D mzids search fixed Carbamidomethyl C and variable +79.96633 S/T/Y (Phospho, UNIMOD:21) in both protocols, missedCleavages -1.

mzXML msInstrument msModel "Orbitrap Fusion" (parentFile G:\Fusion_data\... or F:\MS-RAW\...); paper Methods: samples for Fig. 1, Fig. 4d,e and Supplementary Fig. 7 "were run on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid"; PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol also says Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid. PRIDE instruments field says "LTQ Orbitrap" (MS:1000449) - contradicted by raw metadata and protocol; raw wins.
ms2 header ActivationType CID; paper "CID fragmentation" / "CID MS/MS in the ion trap".

Paper Methods: "operated in a data dependent mode" (Fusion) / "operated in data-dependent mode" (Q Exactive); ms2 headers "AcquisitionMethod Data-Dependent" and filter lines with " d Full ms2".

PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol and paper: "digested overnight with trypsin". mzIdentML Enzyme MS:1001251 Trypsin (search also allowed half-tryptic peptides per paper; recorded here as a note, the digestion enzyme is trypsin, rule 2).

limitations: The WT/HGPS comparison spans two deposits (PXD006015 WT, PXD006016 HGPS); each SDRF carries one disease state.
HGPS_0D_extract heavy fraction (17.9% of passing PSMs) is higher than other 0D runs (0.7-1.8%); not explained in the paper; the file is annotated as named (0 day).

No vendor .raw files are deposited (none of PXD006012-PXD006016 has one); comment[data file] lists the RawConverter .ms2 files that PRIDE categorises as RAW. The .mzXML (PEAK) copies are not listed. Reprocessing from the SDRF will need .ms2/.mzXML-capable tools.

SILAC culture medium is not stated (paper: cells grown in MEM + 15% FBS for general culture; SILAC media base not named) -> characteristics[culture medium] not available. Passage stated only as "<20" -> not available. Storage temperature not stated.
Quiescence (1% serum for 3-5 days before harvest/labelling) applies to every sample and is encoded only in the source names, not as a treatment column.
